messages:
Ishaan: did a quick merge of cust-boreal LoRA onto baseline-large int4 this morning. ran the 'money-format' evalpack and seeing consistent token-split / spacing around decimals and thousands separators. opening thread to triage.
Maya: can you drop the eval link and a minimal repro?
Ishaan: internal eval id: https://redwood.internal/evals/BB207 (private)
Ishaan: repro command:
```bash
tools/quick_eval --model=boreal-lora-merged-int4 --eval=money-format --limit=300 --seed=13 --tokenizer=/mnt/cust/boreal/tokenizer.json --out=/tmp/boreal_out.json
```
Fiona: paste an example pair (baseline vs merged) so we can see detok artifacts
Ishaan: sample:
```text
PROMPT: "Invoice total: $" + total + "\nPlease pay by due date."
BASELINE (fp32): "Invoice total: $7,250.00
Please pay by due date."
MERGED-INT4: "Invoice total: $7,250 .00
Please pay by due date."
```
CS: customer reports intermittent missing comma on higher values too (e.g., "7250" vs "7,250"). overall EM_format went from 98% -> 72% on this pack.
Maya: two suspects: 1) tokenizer mismatch between LoRA training and merge-time tokenizer mapping, 2) int4 quant causing token fragmentation (outlier-sensitive layers).
Fiona: we have a remap tool `remap-lora-tokens` that can transpose LoRA deltas to a different token id map. try rerunning merge with their tokenizer preserved: `remap-lora-tokens --lora=./lora.pt --src-tokenmap=trained.json --dst-tokenmap=/mnt/cust/boreal/tokenizer.json` then rebuild merged weights.
Ishaan: queued a job: "merge-remap-with-cust-tokenizer". ops-bot: queued on `gpu-qa-1` (1xA40), ETA ~20m.
ops-bot: job-id 8921 created, ETA 18m.
Maya: also run a quant ablation: merged-int8 vs merged-int4 vs float32. if int8 matches float32, quant step is suspect.
Ishaan: ran quick ablation (n=500): MAE_amounts: fp32=0.02, int8=0.05, int4=1.83. TokenSplitRate (fraction tokens that split numeric punctuation): fp32=0.002, int8=0.006, int4=0.14.
Fiona: that MAE gap is huge -> quant sensitivity. try per-channel outlier clipping during int4 quant and `--merge-correction=kv-rescale` flag. also rerun detok with `--detok-preserve-number-groups` to debug whether decoder spacing is coming from token boundaries or from detokenizer whitespace heuristics.
Maya: add an eval metric for EM_count_format and a small set of synthetic numeric edgecases (leading zeros, currency symbols, negative amounts). canary these before rolling to customer.
CS: if this affects invoices, we need a quick rollback plan. recommend feature-flagging their model route to int8 fallback and open a support note.
Ishaan: will draft PR for prod-config to add canary route + fallback to int8. also starting the remap+remerge job now. will post artifacts.
Fiona: long term, we should add a token-alignment verification step to the LoRA onboarding checklist: verify token id overlap for numerics and punctuation >99.9% or run automated remap. I'll file a tiny RFC.
Maya: agree. short-term mitigation: remap+remerge or enable int8 per-customer; also consider shipping a decode-time tokenizer shim that maps incoming token ids for that customer only (fast patch).
Ishaan: remerge job done, posting diff artifacts: `diff_tokens.txt` shows 0.6% numeric-token id differences before remap -> 0.0% after. re-eval in progress.
ops-bot: eval job 8930 finished, summary uploaded to /artifacts/8930/summary.json (internal).
Ishaan: new results: EM_format improved 72% -> 96.5% after remap+remerge. int4 MAE_amounts dropped to 0.12. still slightly worse than fp32 but acceptable for rollout.
CS: sharing with customer now, recommending staged canary and monitoring for 24h.
Maya: nice recovery. follow-ups: 1) add token-alignment check to onboarding, 2) add per-customer int4 clipping profile, 3) write up quick KB note for CS.
Fiona: also add automated synthetic numeric tests to our standard evalpacks so this doesn't slip.
Ishaan: thanks team. will close thread after KB + prod-config PR are merged. :white_check_mark:
